topics.description: The major 1524–1525 uprising of peasants and lower-status rural communities in the German lands during the Reformation era.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These people promulgated the Twelve Articles under the leadership of Thomas Muntzer. Martin Luther compared these people to “mad dogs” in a tract titled “Against the Thieving, Murderous Hordes of [these people].” These people carried out a 1525 (*) revolt in Germany, and were likened to the working-class proletariat in an analysis by Friedrich Engels. For 10 points, name this lower class of people in Medieval society.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Swabian (SWAY-bee-en) League participated in ending this conflict, which died down after  Thomas Müntzer was executed after the Battle of Frankenhausen (FRAHN-ken-HOW-zen). For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this 1525 uprising against German landholders that began in Alsace (AL-zass).
parts.answer: Peasants' War [or German Peasants' War of 1525; or Deutscher Bauernkrieg; do not  accept or prompt on “Peasants' Revolt”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This group believed in delaying a central Christian ritual until adulthood and influenced the  Peasants' War. The Amish and Mennonites are sects of this group.
parts.answer: Anabaptists [or Radical Reformers; do not accept or prompt on “Reformers” or  “Protestants”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: A German knight who fought on the peasant side, Götz von Berlichingen (GUTS von BUR-leh-shin￾in), was nicknamed for using one of these medical devices following a maiming injury at the 1504 siege  of Landshut (LANDZ-hood).
parts.answer: iron hand [or artificial hand; or artificial limb; or prosthesis; or prosthetic hand; or Götz  of the Iron Hand; Götz von der Eisernen Hand]

topics.description: The Habsburg ruler who was Holy Roman Emperor and king of Spain during the first half of the sixteenth century.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This empire’s “Great Interregnum” ended with the ascension of the House of Luxembourg. Local leaders  of this empire met in the Imperial Diet. Within this empire, France rivaled the Hapsburgs for influence with  its (*) electors. This empire was ruled by Spanish kings in the 1500s after the election of Charles V. For 10 points,  name this fragmented Central European empire, which ruled much of medieval Germany.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Residents of this country’s colonies that were born in this country were called peninsulares. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country which colonized most of Latin America aside from Brazil.
parts.answer: Spain [or Kingdom of Spain; or Reino de Espana]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Spanish crown gave grants of forced native labor to landowners in this system. Due to the shift to  agricultural activity in the Spanish colonies, this system was succeeded by the hacienda system.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This ruler passed the New Laws in an attempt to mitigate the exploitation of the encomienda system. This  Spanish king and Holy Roman Emperor was succeeded by Phillip II.
parts.answer: Charles V [accept Charles I of Spain; accept Carlos V; or Carlos I; prompt on Charles or Carlos]

topics.description: Monumental pyramid-shaped structures built by multiple ancient civilizations for religious, ceremonial, or funerary purposes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This city was burned down in the 550s during a peasant revolt. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this “birthplace of the gods,” later sacked by the Toltecs for good measure. This city was home to the  Avenue of the Dead.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Teotihuacan was home to two of these structures, which were named for the sun and moon. Djoser constructed  “step” varieties of these structures.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Teotihuacan was situated in this country, though it was often more interested in exerting its influence south of  this modern-day country’s border with Guatemala.
parts.answer: Mexico [or United Mexican States; or Estados Unidos Mexicanos]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The general Siyaj K’ak’ overthrew the king of this city in 378 CE and replaced him with a ruler from Teotihuacan. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Mayan city in modern-day Guatemala that was home to the Lost World complex. This city fought a series of wars with the rival city of Calakmul.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Tikal’s Lost World Complex was centered on one of these structures. Teotihuacan was home to two of these structures named for the Sun and Moon, and the ancient Egyptians built a “Great” one of these structures at Giza.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Mayans also constructed a pyramid named El Castillo, or the Temple of Kukulcán, in this city. This city in the Yucatán peninsula also contained the Great Ball Court.

topics.description: Monumental ancient Egyptian funerary structures built primarily as tombs for pharaohs and other elites, including the pyramids of Giza and Djoser’s Step Pyramid.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of these religious structures has a “Cannibal Hymn” inscribed on its walls as part of a “Text” named for these places, and was built for Teti. One of these structures near Saqqara was built for Djoser [JOH-sur] by Imhotep. (*) Mastabas were a “stepped” type of these structures, three of which were built for rulers like Khafre and Khufu near Giza. For ten points, name this large, imposing kind of structure where Egyptian pharaohs were buried.
parts.answer: pyramids (accept pyramids of Giza; accept descriptions of specific pyramids, such as the Pyramid of Teti, Djoser, Menkaure, Khafre, and/or Khufu; prompt on more general terms like “tomb,” “necropolis,” or “burial place”)

topics.description: An ancient Roman city near the Gulf of Naples destroyed and preserved by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Pliny the Younger wrote an account of how he fled the destruction of this city and how his uncle, Pliny the Elder, didn’t escape. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this city that was destroyed by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius, burying its citizens under a thick layer of ash.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Many walls in the ruins of ancient Pompeii are covered in these messages; for example, two men named Gaius and Aulus announced that they “were here” with this illicit type of wall art.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Like Pompeii, this rich seaside city was destroyed and well preserved by Vesuvius’s ash. The Villa of the Papyri can be found in this city’s ruins.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The ruins of this city include a series of initiation frecoes at the Villa of the Mysteries. The Alexander Mosaic was excavated from the House of the Faun in this city, where the discovery of graffiti allowed scholars to refine their understanding of Vulgar Latin. Stabiae [stab-ee-eye] and Herculaneum were devastated along with this town on the Gulf of Naples in 79 CE. For ten points, name this ancient Roman city that was buried under the ash of Mount Vesuvius.

topics.description: Ivan IV's system of separately governed territories and political repression, including the armed forces used to purge perceived opponents during the 1560s and 1570s.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This ruler commissioned the construction of St. Basil's Cathedral to celebrate the capture of Kazan. This man created the oprichniki secret police, which he used to sack the city of Novgorod and purge the (*) Russian nobility. The "Chosen Council" appointed this man as the first Tsar of Russia. For 10 points, name this 16th-century monarch popularly named for his brutality.
parts.answer: Ivan IV Vasilyevich [or Ivan Vasilyevich or Ivan the Terrible or Ivan the Formidable or Ivan the Fearsome or Ivan the Awesome or Ivan Grozny; prompt on Ivan]

topics.description: The special corps established by Ivan the Terrible to enforce the Oprichnina through political repression, confiscations, and violence.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This ruler created a parliament called the Zemsky Sobor in 1549. Three people claimed to be this ruler’s dead youngest son, Dmitri, during the Time of Troubles. Peasants were terrorized and the city of (*) Novgorod was sacked by the Oprichniki, this ruler’s secret police. This man the epithet “Grozny” from acts like beating his own son to death. For ten points, name this first Tsar of All Russia, known as “the Terrible.”
parts.answer: Ivan the Terrible (accept Ivan IV Vasilyevich; accept Ivan the Fearsome, Ivan the Awesome, or anything similar; accept Ivan Grozny)

topics.description: The modern Central European country commonly known as Germany, including references to its geography, culture, and history when the answer is the country rather than a specifically named historical state.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: At a conference held in this country, Portugal presented the “Pink Map,” which was approved by all attendees except Britain, to handle claims in southern Africa. This empire, which was unified by a statesman who claimed “Politics is the art of the possible” in describing his philosophy of (*) Realpolitik, included states like Schleswig, Holstein, and Prussia. Otto von Bismarck helped unify, for ten points, what European country where Kaisers Wilhelm I [first] and II [second] led from Berlin?
parts.answer: Germany (accept German Empire; accept Deutsches Kaiserreich or Deutsches Reich; do not accept or prompt on “Prussia”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country that was home to a 1937 exhibition of so-called “degenerate art.” That exhibition mocked artworks that were part of some movements in this country like New Objectivity.
parts.answer: Germany [or Federal Republic of Germany or Bundesrepublik Deutschland; accept West Germany or Nazi Germany or the Third Reich]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Like many contemporary German artists, Anselm Kiefer’s work is heavily inspired by this World War II era genocide that killed two thirds of Europe’s Jewish population.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Although he was an ardent Nazi, the most-exhibited artist at the Degenerate Art Exhibition was Emil Nolde, a member of this movement. Another artist from this movement showed himself in his studio with one hand amputated in Self-Portrait as a Soldier.
parts.answer: Die Brücke [or The Bridge] (Self-Portrait as a Soldier is by Ernst Kirchner.)

topics.description: The former socialist German state that existed from 1949 until German reunification in 1990.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about Ostalgie [OHSS-tal-gee], for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Ostalgie is nostalgia for things made in this country. The “chemical breakdown” tactics of psychological torture were used by this country’s Stasi secret police.
parts.answer: East Germany [or German Democratic Republic; or GDR; or Deutsche Demokratische Republik; or DDR; reject “West Germany”; reject “Federal Republic of Germany”; reject “Germany” alone]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Ostalgie includes a fondness for one of these products called Vita. In Nazi Germany, a formula for this product called Fanta was created after a trade embargo with Coke.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A caricature of this leader in a straw hat appeared on East German traffic lights and is appreciated by Ostalgie enjoyers. This last head of state of East Germany was depicted kissing Leonid Brezhnev in a Berlin Wall mural.

topics.description: The democratic West German state aligned with the Western Bloc from 1949 until reunification with East Germany in 1990.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s first Chancellor, Konrad Adenauer (AH-den-ow-er), presided over its economic miracle, which is also called Wirtschaftswunder (veer-CHAHFTS-voonder) or the Miracle on the Rhine. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country which was part of the Western Bloc during the Cold War. Willy Brandt, a leader of this country, championed its philosophy of Ostpolitik which sought to normalize relations with its eastern neighbor.
parts.answer: West Germany [accept Federal Republic of Germany or FRG or BRD or Bonn Republic; prompt on Germany; do not accept or prompt on “East Germany” or “German Democratic Republic” or “GDR” or “DDR”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Willy Brandt’s government toppled when it was revealed that one of his advisors, Gunter Guillaume, was an agent for this organization. This organization was the secret police force of East Germany.
parts.answer: Stasi [accept Ministry for State Security or State Security Service]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Although this city was fully inside East Germany, it was separated into West and East portions by an eponymous wall. This city is the current capital of Germany.
